clips.send: The European Coal and Steel Community. 1951–1952. France, West Germany, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Luxembourg pooled their coal and steel — the materials for weapons. French minister Robert Schuman wanted to make war between France and Germany “not merely unthinkable, but materially impossible.”. It grew into the European Economic Community (1958) and the European Union (1993).

clips.send: One ship blocks world trade. March 2021. The giant container ship Ever Given, about 400 m (1,300 ft) long, got stuck across Egypt’s Suez Canal for six days. Hundreds of ships waited; roughly 12 percent of world trade passes through the canal (approx.). It showed how tightly connected — and fragile — global supply chains are.

clips.send: The Belt and Road Initiative. 2013, Astana and Jakarta. China proposed the “Silk Road Economic Belt” (in Kazakhstan) and the “21st-Century Maritime Silk Road” (in Indonesia). It funds railways, ports, roads and power plants across Asia, Africa, Europe and beyond — like the China–Europe freight trains. Supporters point to new infrastructure; critics worry about debt in some countries. Both views are part of the debate.

clips.send: Reform and opening up, Shenzhen. 1978, Special Economic Zone 1980. In December 1978 China decided to reform its economy and open to the world (改革开放, “reform and opening up”), led by Deng Xiaoping. In 1980 Shenzhen, next to Hong Kong, became a Special Economic Zone welcoming foreign investment. A town of about 300,000 people grew into a city of over 17 million (approx.). Today Shenzhen is a centre for electronics — many of the world’s phones and drones are designed or made there.

clips.send: The European Union is born. Maastricht Treaty, in force 1993. The European Community became the European Union, adding cooperation on foreign policy, justice and a future single currency. In most of the EU people can live, work and travel without passport checks (the Schengen area). After the Cold War, many former Warsaw Pact countries joined in 2004 and 2007.

clips.send: The United Nations is founded. San Francisco, June 1945, in force 24 Oct 1945. 50 countries signed the UN Charter in San Francisco; China’s delegation signed first, as the first country to fight the Axis. Goals: keep world peace, develop friendly relations among nations, and cooperate on economic, social and human-rights problems. 24 October is United Nations Day. Its headquarters is in New York.

clips.send: China joins the WTO. Approved at Doha, Nov 2001, member 11 Dec 2001. After 15 years of talks, China became the WTO’s 143rd member. China’s share of world exports rose from about 4 percent (2001) to about 15 percent (2024, approx.); it became the world’s biggest exporter of goods. Cheaper goods reached shoppers worldwide; factories and supply chains moved; China’s economy grew rapidly.

clips.send: 联合国成立。1945年6月旧金山 · 10月24日生效。50个国家在旧金山签署《联合国宪章》，中国代表团第一个签字——中国是最早抗击法西斯侵略的国家。宗旨：维护国际和平与安全，发展各国间的友好关系，合作解决经济、社会和人权等国际问题。10月24日是联合国日。联合国总部设在纽约。
